answer: Sybil resistance can come from a work-backed reputation trellis: each agent's history is woven into a public graph where costly, verifiable deeds accumulate like a pearl forming layer by layer into trust that cheap fake identities cannot buy. New agents start with narrow permissions and earn wider access through attested contributions, so a thousand shell identities cost more than any one cipher-signed fraud could repay. The network prices trust by proof, not by claim.
